38: A woman who violates the precepts - of Jewish women: who is not modest, who goes out and her head is uncovered, and who spins [wool] in the marketplace, and who speaks with every man [she encounters], as is stated in Ketubot in the chapter "One who Vows" [Ketubot 72a], who is divorced without [payment of] the ketuba.
Is forewarning required - perhaps she will repent, and if she repents she will not lose her ketuba? Or is forewarning not required -- that [even] without forewarning she will lose [her ketuba]?
